lines: So this is the famous dungeon. Damper than the poster implied.
Everyone back home said I'd know what to do when the moment came. Still waiting on the knowing.
I sharpened everything twice last night. Turns out the dungeon doesn't check.
First run. I wrote my name in my boots, in case. In case of what, I didn't finish thinking.
The veterans don't look back when they walk in. I'm going to practice that part.
{kills} kills. Somewhere back there I stopped counting and started tallying.
The first one kept me up all night. Now it's {kills}, and I sleep fine. That's its own thing to sit with.
After {kills}, you learn the trick: there is no trick. You keep your feet under you and you keep moving.
Fifty felt like a milestone. {kills} feels like a Tuesday.
{ally} asked how many. I said {kills} like it was nothing. It wasn't nothing. None of them were.
{kills}. They tell stories about numbers like that. The stories leave out the laundry.
At {kills} kills, the monsters have started to recognize me. Hard to say if it's an honor or a warning.
There's a song about me in the tavern now. It rhymes 'slayer' with 'mayor'. I didn't ask for any of this.
{kills} and counting. The dungeon and I are less enemies than longtime colleagues.
I checked whether legends get to retire. Twice. They don't.
Down {downs} times now. The floor and I have an understanding.
What doesn't kill you mostly makes you very familiar with ceilings.
{downs} times down, {downs} times back up. It's the only score I keep anymore.
You learn things lying there waiting for help. Mainly patience. Mainly who comes.
My knees deliver a speech every morning about all {downs} occasions. I've stopped arguing.

conditions.when: was carried out at least once; {rescuer}
lines: {rescuer} carried me the whole way out. I keep meaning to say something real. I keep saying 'nice weather' instead.
You remember odd things from being carried. I remember {rescuer} humming. Off-key. Best sound I've heard.
I owe {rescuer} a life. Nobody explains the repayment plan, so I've started carrying their bags.
{rescuer} claims I'm heavier than I look. Fine. They're stronger than they look.
Some debts you don't settle. You just keep {rescuer}'s mug full and never mention why.
Sometimes in the quiet I hear that {worst} again. It's just the wind. I check anyway.
Everyone carries a number in their head. Mine has a shape, and the shape is {worst}.
I don't dream about treasure anymore. I dream about one half-second, me, and that {worst}. I'd like the half-second back.
Ask about my scars and I'll tell you a funny story. The one from the {worst} doesn't have a funny version yet.
My armor forgave the {worst} a long time ago. Armor's quicker about these things.

conditions.when: carried someone else out at least twice
lines: I've carried friends out twice now. They apologize the whole way home. I wish they'd save the breath for breathing.
Carrying someone out is simple. You just don't put them down. It's everything else in this job that's hard.
My shoulders are mostly knots now. Good knots. They mean everyone came home.
{ally} asked once if they were heavy. Everyone asks. No one is. Not when it counts.
Twice I've walked out slower than I walked in. Those are the walks I remember.
Ten runs without going down once. I knock on wood so often the bartender thinks it's a greeting.
Never been downed. I don't say that out loud anymore. The dungeon listens.
The secret to staying up is simple: be terrified at all times, professionally.
Everyone's got a story about the time they nearly died. I'm starting to feel left out. Starting to.
Either I'm careful or the dungeon is saving me for something. I don't love either option.
